title: Tech Note: IIS and ISAPI REWRITE
author: Timothy Penner, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Helicon Tech ISAPI_Rewrite filter (3rd-party reverse proxy/URL rewriter)
SOAP request routing via reverse proxy

historical_commentary.text: This note explained how to front 4D's built-in web server with Microsoft IIS using the 3rd-party Helicon ISAPI_Rewrite filter, mainly to satisfy corporate IT departments that insisted on IIS. The general need — fronting 4D's web server with a standard reverse proxy for corporate compliance, SSL termination, or URL rewriting — is still valid and unremarkable today, but the specific tool (a now largely legacy ISAPI filter) has been overtaken by more modern, actively maintained reverse-proxy options (IIS's own URL Rewrite module, nginx, or a cloud/CDN-based proxy), and the SOAP-specific routing examples reflect a web-services approach 4D has since moved beyond with REST and ORDA.
related_updates: Microsoft's own free URL Rewrite Module for IIS has since become the standard native way to achieve this instead of the 3rd-party Helicon ISAPI_Rewrite filter
REST + ORDA (4D v16 R5+, 2017) has largely superseded SOAP as 4D's recommended web services approach, making the SOAP-specific proxy examples less relevant today
Reverse proxying 4D's web server behind IIS, nginx, or a cloud load balancer remains a common and still-relevant deployment pattern
